events.content: STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. This is terrible news for Sarah. I need to offer my condolences first. The deadline is a huge problem, but that can wait a moment. The human thing to do is express sympathy.
I'm so sorry to hear that, Sarah.
Waiting to see how Sarah or the others respond.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Jun Jie is being nice. I should thank him. The real issue is the deadline. I need to tell them I'll be away. The wake is tonight and the funeral is tomorrow. It's my duty to be with my family. I have to be direct about it.
Thanks, Jun Jie. The wake is tonight, and the funeral is tomorrow. I have to be with my family.
I've stated my situation and now I'm waiting for the team's response.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Okay, she's confirmed she'll be out today and tomorrow. That's completely understandable. But her work isn't done and the pitch is Thursday morning. I'm the lead, I have to bring this up. We have to figure out how the rest of us can finish her section. I'll state the problem plainly so we can start talking about a solution.
Of course. You need to be with your family. This does put us in a difficult position for the Thursday deadline, though.
Waiting for the team to respond to the problem I've raised.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Jun Jie has brought up the deadline, which is the main problem. He's not being aggressive, just stating a fact. I need to show I understand the pressure we're under but also that my family obligation is firm. Proposing a way to get the work done is the best way to handle this. It shows I'm responsible and not just leaving them with the problem. I can work tonight after the wake.
I know, and I'm sorry about the timing. I can work on it tonight after I get home.
I've offered a solution. Now I'll wait to see how they respond.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Sarah's offering to work after her grandmother's wake. That's not realistic. She'll be exhausted and emotionally drained. We can't count on that, and it's not right to ask her. The only practical solution is for the rest of us to take over her work. I need to tell her not to worry and that we'll handle it. This puts the ball in our court to figure out the logistics.
Don't worry about that, Sarah. You need to be with your family. The three of us will cover your section.
I have made a proposal to solve the workload issue. Now I wait for the team's reaction.
STRATEGY: ASSERT. Jun Jie just volunteered me for more work without asking. I can't do it. I'm already overloaded covering for Wei and working late. I need to speak up immediately.
Hang on, Jun Jie. I can't take on more. I'm already covering for Wei.
I've stated my position and now I'll wait for a response.

STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Hui Min just said she can't take on more work. My initial proposal of the three of us splitting Sarah's section is unworkable. I need to find out what the remaining capacity is. The next logical step is to ask Shu Fen about her workload.
Okay, you're right. I forgot about Wei. Shu Fen, what's your workload like?
Waiting for Shu Fen's response to assess our team's capacity.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Jun Jie is asking me to take on extra work. I can't. My own section is already behind schedule. If I take on Sarah's analysis, which I've never done before, I'll either do a bad job on it or fall even further behind on my own part. Either way, I'll get blamed if things go wrong. I have to be direct and say I can't do it.
I'm behind on my own section. I can't take on any more.
I have answered the question and stated my position.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Okay, so nobody can cover for me. Jun Jie's idea didn't work. This brings it back to my offer. I need to make it clear that I'm not just leaving them with the problem. I'll work on it myself.
I can still work on it tonight. After I get back from the wake.
I've repeated my offer as it seems to be the only solution now.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Sarah is offering to work again, but I already told her not to. It's not a good idea for her to work after her grandmother's wake. It's unreliable and not fair to her. Since Hui Min and Shu Fen can't take on the work, it looks like it's down to me. I'm the lead, so the responsibility falls on me to get this done. I need to make it clear that she should not worry and that I will handle it.
No, Sarah. You need to be with your family. Don't worry about the pitch. I'll cover your section.
I've offered to take on the work myself. Now waiting to see the team's reaction.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Jun Jie's offer is very kind, but it's not realistic. I just heard Hui Min and Shu Fen say they are at capacity. He can't do my section plus his own. The pitch will be at risk, and it will be my fault. I need to thank him but make it clear that his solution isn't possible and insist on my own. I can't let him take this on alone.
I appreciate that, Jun Jie, but you can't do it all by yourself. I'll work on it tonight when I get home. It's okay, really.
I've challenged his unrealistic offer and repeated my own practical solution.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. This is the third time Sarah has offered to work while she should be grieving. It's admirable but not realistic or reliable. The project's success can't depend on someone working after their grandmother's wake. As the lead, I need to be firm, end this discussion, and make it clear that the decision is made. She needs to focus on her family, and I will handle the work.
Sarah, I mean it. The work is handled. Please, just be with your family.
I have made my final decision on the matter clear.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. How is the work 'handled'? Jun Jie just heard that both Shu Fen and I are at capacity. He can't possibly do his own section plus Sarah's half-finished one all by himself before Thursday. He's just trying to be nice, but it's not realistic and it's going to cause problems for all of us later.
How is it handled, Jun Jie? You can't do your part and all of her part by yourself.
I've pointed out the flaw in Jun Jie's plan. Now I'll see how he responds.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Hui Min has a valid point. I told Sarah it was handled, and now I'm being asked how. I need to show I'm not just making empty statements. I'm the lead, the buck stops with me. If no one else can do it, then I have to. The only way is to put in more hours.
I'll work late tonight and come in early. It will get done.
I've explained my plan. Now waiting for a response.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Jun Jie's solution is just to work himself to death. That's not a plan, it's a way to get sloppy work done, if it gets done at all. The quality of the whole pitch is at risk if one major section is rushed by someone who's exhausted. I need to point this out.
That's not a plan. What happens if the work isn't good because you're exhausted?
I've challenged the quality risk of his plan and am waiting for a response.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Hui Min is right. If Jun Jie tries to do it all himself, the quality of the work will suffer. A bad final pitch reflects on all of us, and I don't want to be blamed for that. I should back her up. It shows I'm concerned about the project's success, not just avoiding work.
She has a point. We can't risk the quality of the whole pitch.
I've supported Hui Min's concern about the quality of the work.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Hui Min and Shu Fen are both questioning my plan. They're right to be concerned about quality. Just saying 'I'll work hard' isn't enough. I need to give them a reason to believe the quality won't suffer. Proposing a review by them is a good way to address their concern directly and show I'm not just being stubborn. It makes them part of the solution.
I understand the concern. But the work has to be done, and I'm the only one who can do it. The quality will not suffer. I'll have it ready for you both to review tomorrow.
I've addressed their quality concerns and proposed a review. Now waiting for their reaction.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Jun Jie is just brushing off the risk. A review tomorrow is cutting it way too close. If his work is a mess because he's overworked, we won't have time to fix it before the deadline on Thursday morning. He's not thinking about the team, just about being the hero.
And if we review it tomorrow and it's not right? We'll have no time to fix it.
I've pointed out the biggest flaw in his plan: the lack of time for corrections.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Hui Min's point is exactly what I'm worried about. If we get bad work from Jun Jie tomorrow, we're all stuck. There's no time to fix it, and the whole project will be weak. My main goal is to not get blamed for that. I can't take on Sarah's work, and neither can Hui Min. But Sarah herself offered to work tonight. Maybe that's the solution. If she can do even a little, it reduces the risk of Jun Jie being overwhelmed and doing a bad job. It's a practical way forward.
She's right. There won't be time to fix it. Sarah said she could work tonight. Maybe that's what we should do, let her do what she can.
I've proposed a potential solution to the workload and quality risk issue.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Shu Fen is bringing up letting Sarah work again. I've already said no to this multiple times. It's not a reliable plan, and it's not right. We can't stake the project on someone who's grieving. It's a risk to quality and it's not fair to her. I'm the lead, I made a decision, and I need to be firm about it. The discussion is closed.
No. We are not asking Sarah to work. It's not an option. I've already made the decision. I will handle her section.
I have stated my final position on the matter.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Jun Jie is being completely unreasonable and shutting down discussion. He's acting like he's in charge, but he's not. He said, 'I've already made the decision.' That's not his call to make alone. This is a team project, and his plan puts all of our work at risk. If he messes this up, we all look bad. My main priority is to not get blamed for bad work, and letting him run off and do a rush job on a critical section is the fastest way for that to happen. I need to push back on the idea that he can just decide this for everyone.
This isn't just your decision to make. The risk is for the whole team.
I've challenged Jun Jie's authority to make a unilateral decision and stated the collective risk.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. They're all arguing because of me. Jun Jie's plan to do everything himself isn't going to work, and Hui Min and Shu Fen are right to be worried about the risk to the pitch. It's my responsibility. I've already said I can work tonight, and Shu Fen just brought it up again. I need to step in and say it one more time, firmly. It's the only way to solve this, so I can be with my family and the work still gets done properly.

Jun Jie, I really appreciate you trying to help, but they have a point. It's not fair to put all of it on you. This is my section. Let me do it. I'll go to the wake, and I'll finish my work when I get home tonight. It's the safest way.
I have restated my proposal, which seems to be the most logical solution to the team's impasse.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Everyone is against my decision, even Sarah. They think letting her work while grieving is the 'safest' option. It's absolutely not. It's the riskiest. I'm the lead, and I have to make the final call on how we manage this risk. I will not put this project's success on the shoulders of someone who has just lost a family member. It's both a bad project decision and the wrong thing to do to a colleague. I need to end this debate now.

Sarah, with all due respect, that is not the safest way. It's the riskiest. We cannot base our delivery on the hope that you'll be able to work after your grandmother's wake. It's not a reliable plan. My decision stands. I am doing the work. This discussion is over.
I have unequivocally stated my final decision and the reasoning behind it.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Who does he think he is, saying 'this discussion is over'? This is a team project, not his personal dictatorship. The risk falls on all of us if he messes this up. He can't just unilaterally decide something so critical.
You don't get to just decide that for everyone, Jun Jie. It's a team project.
I've challenged his authority to make a unilateral decision. Let's see how he responds to that.
